To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we cloned the entire coding sequence for murine gamma-interferon and that we expressed the gene in a mammalian cell line.
we have cloned the complete coding sequence for MuIFN-gam

a complete cDNA clone encoding the murine interferon (IFN)-gamma protein has been isolated, expressed in a variety of heterologous cell lines, and used as a probe to identify and characterize a murine IFN-gamma genomic clone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cloning and expression of a murine interferon cDNA.
the cloning of the murine IFN-gamma gene and the development of a stable cell line that constitutively expresses IFN-gamma.
the molecular cloning and characterization of a complete cDNA for murine interferon- gamma (IFN-gamma).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cloned interferon gene is the same as the natural one.
MuIFN-gammas are produced in the same way as MuIFN-gammab.
the interferon activity produced by the transformed cell clones was identical to the natural, splenocytes-derived interferon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cDNA sequence for the murine interferon, which we have now determined, and which has been deposited in GenBank, contains 5' untranslated regions of 63 and 40 bases, a single intron of 105 bases, and 3' untranslated regions of approximately 1,000 bases.
a complete cDNA clone was obtained and that it was successfully used in heterologous expression systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we were able to clone the cDNA for mouse IFN-gamma.

we can produce large quantities of interferon in a mammalian cell line that is easy to grow and maintain, and that the interferon produced is indistinguishable from the interferon that we can get from the spleen.
we have shown the ability to produce a recombinant interferon in heterologous cells, which is a key step in the development of an efficient system for the large scale production of this protein.
